newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe war veterans loot ruling party office.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe war veterans loot ruling party office.

text.p: Zimbabwean independence war veterans stormed and looted the headquarters of President Robert Mugabe's ruling ZANU-PF party on Wednesday night, local state media reported on Thursday.
The daily Herald newspaper said about 100 ex-combatants ransacked the party offices in Harare, cutting telephone lines, looting food and cigarettes and briefly holding some office workers hostage.
It was the latest incident in a campaign by the veterans -- heroes of a 1970s guerrilla war that won the southern African state independence in 1980 -- to win compensation from the government.
The government suspended the general war victims' compensation fund in March to ease investigations into charges the fund had been heavily defrauded, including by some cabinet members.
Mugabe has set up a judicial commission to probe the allegations, and his government is only paying out compensation on a slow, case-by-case basis.

The war veterans have staged a series of spectacular protests around the country in the last two months, demanding unconditional release of their claims and a meeting with Mugabe, who is patron of their representative Zimbabwe National Liberation War Veterans Association.
Mugabe says he will only meet them when he has "the full facts".

The Herald said the veterans were violent on Wednesday, threatening journalists and assaulting some policemen. The state news agency ZIANA said some of the ex-combatants urinated around the party offices where they smashed furniture.
"Police officers on the ground felt that arresting the demonstrators at the scene would trigger more violence," the Herald said.
It quoted a senior police officer as saying: "The situation is dangerous. We also have lives to protect".
